changes.before: If the worker sends 8 instead, what prints?
changes.after: Pass one value through an unbuffered channel.

before: make(chan int) creates an unbuffered channel. A send ch <- value and a receive <-ch rendezvous; the sender cannot finish the send until a receiver is ready. Channels communicate typed values, not arbitrary shared memory transactions.

The worker sends one integer, then closes a separate completion channel. main receives the value and waits for done so the worker’s lifetime is complete before returning. Closing the data channel is unnecessary when the receiver knows exactly one value is expected.

Complete local Go example; the app itself does not execute it:
```go
package main

import (
"fmt"
)


func main() {
    values := make(chan int)
    done := make(chan struct{})
    go func() { values <- 6; close(done) }()
    value := <-values
    <-done
    fmt.Println(value * 2)
}
```
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why sending on the same unbuffered channel before any receiver can run would block. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An unbuffered channel has no space to store waiting values. `values <- 6` sends an integer. `<-values` receives it. The send cannot finish until a receiver is ready.
The worker sends one value, then closes a separate done channel. main receives the number and waits for done. It knows exactly one number is expected, so it does not need a close signal on values.

Follow the number from the sender to the receiver.
```go
package main

import (
"fmt"
)


func main() {
    values := make(chan int)
    done := make(chan struct{})
    go func() { values <- 6; close(done) }()
    value := <-values
    <-done
    fmt.Println(value * 2)
}
```
The screen shows `12`. main receives 6 and doubles it.
If no receiver can run, an unbuffered send waits. Here the worker and main can reach opposite sides of the same transfer.
